title: Bridging GenAI policy and practice: Brief instruction improves learning-oriented prompting in an introductory programming course
abstract: arXiv:2602.16033v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is now commonplace in higher education, yet unguided use can harm learning. Universities have responded with policies asking students to use GenAI for learning, not solutions, but how to translate these policies into classroom instruction remains untested. Here we report a randomized controlled trial with a six-week, end-of-semester follow-up (N = 431) in an introductory programming course comparing four instructional approaches, from a two-sentence reminder (Condition 1) to a multi-step constructive task (Condition 4). We found: (1) all four approaches produced learning-oriented prompting gains that persisted six weeks later and scaled with the designed engagement level, from 8 to 51 percentage points; (2) students in every condition self-reported sustained voluntary use, and confidence grew in step with skill; and (3) final examination performance did not differ between conditions, p

translated_title: 弥合生成式AI政策与课堂实践的差距：简短指导改善了编程入门课程中以学习为导向的提示行为
translated_abstract: 生成式人工智能在高等教育中已十分普遍，但缺乏指导的使用可能会损害学习。各大学已出台政策，要求学生将生成式AI用于学习而非直接获取答案，但如何将这些政策转化为课堂教学仍未经检验。我们在一门编程入门课程中开展了一项随机对照试验，并进行了为期六周的学期末随访（N = 431），比较了四种教学干预方法，其强度从两句话的提醒（条件1）到多步骤的建构性任务（条件4）。我们发现：（1）所有四种方法都带来了以学习为导向的提示行为的提升，且该提升在六周后依然持续，并随设计的参与程度递增，提升幅度从8到51个百分点；（2）所有条件下的学生均自我报告持续自愿使用生成式AI，且信心随技能同步增长；（3）各条件之间的期末考试成绩没有显著差异。
tldr: 一项针对431名编程课学生的随机对照试验表明，即使是简短如两句话的课堂指导，也能有效引导学生以学习为导向使用生成式AI，且效果可持续六周、随参与深度递增。
en_tdlr: A randomized controlled trial with 431 introductory programming students shows that even a brief two-sentence classroom instruction effectively guides students toward learning-oriented GenAI prompting, with effects persisting six weeks and scaling with engagement depth.
